answer: One concrete defense is a bonded stake that each agent must anchor to a costly, non-refundable deposit before it can transact. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, making a sybil swarm as uneconomical as planting a farm on frozen tundra. An honest agent recovers its bond through sustained useful work, while a throwaway attacker, bright and brief like a comet, forfeits everything the moment its fakes are slashed.
